open_points.subject: store.read_records argument-validation error behavior
open_points.text: "A call that passes other arguments is a defect of its caller and answers `internal_error` — so does one that omits an argument its relation names or passes one of another kind" vs `public_op:store.read_records` "Errors: `unknown_reference` for the whole call when any named identity does not exist"
open_points.question: For `store.read_records`, is invalid relation argument shape part of the public error contract (returning `internal_error`), or should callers assume only `unknown_reference` is possible?
options: Include `internal_error` explicitly in `public_op:store.read_records` for malformed relation arguments
Forbid such calls by contract and treat behavior as undefined/defect outside API
open_points.default_guess: Return `internal_error` as stated in the relation section, even though the per-operation Errors list omits it.

open_points.subject: Actor attribution for automatic writes during request-driven run advancement
open_points.text: State 5 convention: "Every operation that writes a record receives the acting Actor M27 ... from its caller"; State 0 boundary: "its records name it as the actor, so no automatic step looks like a human decision."
open_points.question: When `runs.start_run`, `runs.continue_after_approval`, `runs.continue_after_resolution`, or `runs.resume_run` trigger automatic node progression and write trace/run-progress records, should those writes be attributed to the request actor or to `kernel`?
options: Attribute all writes in the operation to the request actor
Attribute automatic progression writes to `kernel`, keeping only explicit human decisions under owner/agent
open_points.default_guess: Use request actor for request-scoped writes except startup recovery, because State 5 passes actor through operation calls and startup is the only explicit no-actor exception.
